title: Fylgja bundle manifest v6 — the probes’ synthesized hosts, their links and ports under provenance synthesized
description: From M6’s v2: bundle_version was 3 at M7 (D-025 and its M6 notes) and is 4 at M12 (below). `fidelity.production_forwarding` is an object, one entry per platform in the bundle keyed by its package id, so a mixed bundle asserts each platform’s forwarding and M1’s fidelity.forwarding.mixed refusal retires; `mapping[].node_name` is on every row (null on a row without a port) and `fidelity.lossy` is always present ([] when empty), ending M6’s one exception to the empty-list rule; every node gains `bootstrap` {file, via}: the bootstrap file the bundle carries for it and whether containerlab applies it at deploy (startup_config, the topology names it) or the push sends its lines before the artifact’s (push, the topology node has no startup-config; M7). A v2 or v1 bundle is refused by `twin provision` as bundle.version.unsupported naming both versions. Everything else is v2’s. From M5’s v2, bundle_version still 2 at M6: a mapping row may carry `node_name`, the node’s own name for its port, present only where it differs from `interface`; `fidelity.lossy` records every lossy mapping and every shared port, present only when it has content; omissions gain the rule omit.interface.shared. Both fields are the one deliberate exception to M1’s rule that every empty list is emitted as []: a bundle with nothing lossy in it is byte-identical to M5’s, so the goldens and both fixture ids stand and no following twin is rebuilt by the upgrade. The exception expires with M7’s bundle_version bump for per-platform forwarding (D-025), which makes both fields unconditional in the same move. From v1: bundle_version is 2, and every node gains `artifact`, the configuration file the bundle carries for it beside its bootstrap (M5). A v1 bundle is refused by `twin provision` as bundle.version.unsupported naming both versions. Nothing of Infrahub’s — artifact, storage or definition identifiers, a time of generation — appears, so bundle_id moves for the artifact’s bytes or name and for nothing else. Everything else is v1’s. M12: bundle_version is 4. Every mapping row carries enabled, the interface's intent admin state (the CTM's enabled, true when unset), so the bundle says what intent says of each port: twin verify asserts nothing of a cabled port whose row says false, and records the skip. The topology, the bootstrap and every configs file are unchanged by the field. 017 (D-057): bundle_version is 5. The provenance names the scope the read was made under and the mapping that produced the CTM ({reader, model, version}), copied from the CTM envelope, in place of the generics contract’s version; a mapping row loses `iftype`, since every interface of a CTM 2 is a port (configured-not-cabled is an uncabled port); and `fidelity.read` is the CTM envelope’s fidelity list, the reader’s own rows of what it approximated and omitted, copied unchanged by the compiler, which holds no table of any source’s rows. A v4 bundle is refused by `twin provision` as bundle.version.unsupported naming both versions. Everything else is v4’s. 016 (D-064): bundle_version is 6. A snapshot’s probes are compiled into synthesized hosts, one per endpoint, each a node of its probe package’s kind and image cabled by a synthesized link to an uncabled port of the intent. A node carries `provenance` (synthesized; absent on a node of intent, whose provenance is the default) and, for a host, `probe` {name, endpoint, format, package {id, source}} in place of a platform: a host’s `platform`, `psp`, `artifact` and `bootstrap` are null, and `probe` is present exactly when they are, since a host has no support package, no configuration file and no bootstrap (its configuration is its topology node’s exec lines, its package’s host.address and host.route rendered), and its management_port is eth0, containerlab’s. A mapping row and a link carry `provenance` likewise: the host’s own row (its port, cabled) and the device port’s row (cabled, since the synthesized link cables it; intent did not) and the link are synthesized. `probes` records each probe as compiled, sorted by name: its format and package, its two hosts in endpoint order (endpoint, node, device, interface, the host’s port, address, gateway), and its package’s fidelity {forwarding, timing}; `fidelity.synthesized` names every synthesized node, sorted. Both are required and [] when the snapshot declares no probe, so a probe-less snapshot compiles to its v5 bundle but for the version and the two empty lists (R-11). A v5 bundle is refused by `twin provision` as bundle.version.unsupported naming both versions. Everything else is v5’s.

provenance.description: The provenance block: the intent's address, copied from the CTM envelope minus `observed_at` and `fidelity` (which is fidelity.read). Nothing about the read, the host, the clock or the build. 017: `scope` and `mapping` in place of `contract_version`.

at.description: Present iff the operator supplied --at; verbatim.

scope.description: 017: the scope the read was made under, tag:<name>, as the CTM envelope records it.

mapping.description: 017: which reader produced the CTM and which version of which model it read, as the CTM envelope records it.

provenance.description: 016: where the object came from; written only when synthesized, so absent reads as intent.

probe.description: 016: a synthesized host’s probe, in place of a platform: present exactly when platform, psp, artifact and bootstrap are null.

platform.description: The `platform.nos` of the support package the node was built with (017 R-08): a CTM `2` device names its package, not a NOS, and `nos` keys the registry's shadowing of an embedded package by an override. Null on a synthesized host (016).

psp.description: The support package the node was built with; null on a synthesized host (016).

management_port.description: Always the PSP's interfaces.management name: containerlab gives every node one, whether or not intent flags a mgmt_only interface.

artifact.description: The node’s configuration artifact, as the bundle carries it: `file` is its path in the bundle, configs/<node>.<artifact_name>, bytes exactly as Infrahub served them; `checksum` is Infrahub’s own (MD5 hex), verbatim; `size` is the byte count. Null on a synthesized host, which is pushed nothing (016).

bootstrap.description: M7: the node’s bootstrap file, rendered from its package’s template (Constitution IV), and how it reaches the node (the package’s config.bootstrap_via). Null on a synthesized host, whose configuration is its topology node’s exec lines (016).

mapping.description: One row per interface in intent. Sorted by (device, interface). M7: `node_name` on every row. M12: `enabled` on every row. 017: no `iftype`; every interface is a port.

port.description: Node port; null on an omitted row, and only there: every interface of a CTM `2` is a port, so every cabled, management and configured-not-cabled row has one (017, FR-030).

node_name.description: M7: on every row. The node’s own name for the port, as the profile’s rule renders it, equal to `interface` where the platform keeps the production name; null on a row without a port.

enabled.description: M12: the interface's intent admin state (ctm.Interface.enabled, true when unset). On every row from bundle 4. A cabled row with false is still cabled and its bootstrap still enables the port; intent's disabling reaches the node through the artifact (M5), and twin verify asserts nothing of the port or its link.

provenance.description: 016: synthesized on a host’s own row and on the device port a host is cabled to; absent, intent, on every other row.

links.description: Cabled links only. Sorted by id.

provenance.description: 016: synthesized on a host’s link; absent, intent, on a link of intent.

omissions.description: Everything left out and why. Sorted by object then rule. Never empty when the mapping has an 'omitted' row. M6: omit.interface.shared is an uncabled interface whose port a cabled interface of the same device holds; omit.interface.unmappable’s reason now names the rule, placeholder, value and range when a rule matched out of range.

probes.description: 016: each probe as compiled, sorted by name; [] when the snapshot declares none. The lab’s flows and verify’s burst read their probes from here.

hosts.description: The two hosts, a then b.

interface.description: The intent’s port the host is cabled to.

port.description: The host’s own port, its package’s host.interface.

address.description: The host’s address with its prefix length, as declared.

gateway.description: The gateway of the host’s route to the far host, as declared.

fidelity.description: The probe package’s: the hosts forward in software and keep the container’s timing. Asserted, as every fidelity is.

Asserted, never measured (D-022); `basis` says so in the bundle itself (Constitution X). M7: `production_forwarding` per platform; `lossy` always present. 017: `read`, the reader’s fidelity list. 016: `synthesized`.

basis.description: Fidelity is asserted from PSP data and compiler decisions, never measured against production. The only value at M1; a verification layer would add another.

production_forwarding.description: M7 (D-025): one entry per platform in the bundle, keyed by nodes[].psp.id, holding that package’s fidelity.production_forwarding. Keys sorted. Where production forwards in software the twin’s data plane is a fair guide; where in hardware it is not (architecture §1).

lossy.description: M6, unconditional from M7: one entry per interface a lossy rule mapped, and per interface whose port another interface of the same device also renders to, whichever rule; [] when there is none. Sorted by (device, interface). `port` is the rendered port even for an interface the mapping table shows omitted for sharing; `shares` lists every other interface of the device rendering to the port, sorted by interface, with its rule and whether it is cabled. Asserted, like the rest of the block.

node_name.description: the node’s own name for the port, whether or not it differs from the production name

rule.description: the rule’s name, never its position or pattern

lossy.description: whether that rule is declared lossy; false only for an interface recorded because its port is shared

read.description: 017 (Constitution X; FR-029): the CTM envelope’s fidelity list, copied unchanged: one row per field the reader approximated and per source object it omitted, sorted by the whole row, (disposition, object), then source and reason, as the CTM sorts it, so the bundle does not depend on the order its rows arrived in. Beside the packages’ `approximations` and the compiler’s `omitted` and `lossy`; [] only for a reader that wrote none.

object.description: The CTM field approximated (`interface.mgmt_only`, `interface.enabled`, `platform.version`) or the source object omitted (a cable, by its label or its id; a connector that is not a `DcimCable`, by its id).

source.description: The source field or kind the row was read from: `InterfacePhysical.role`, `InterfacePhysical.status`, `DcimPlatform`, `DcimCable`, or the kind of an omitted connector that is not a `DcimCable`.

synthesized.description: 016: every synthesized node, the probes’ hosts, sorted; [] when there is none.

packageRef.description: A package a node was built with: a support package’s platform id, or a probe package’s format, and whether it was the shipped one.
